name: Napoleon
role: First Consul of France (1799–1804) and Emperor of the French (1804–1814, 1815)
summary: Napoleon ruled France as an authoritarian modernizer: he consolidated the Revolution's civil equality and property settlement in the Civil Code and a centralized, merit-oriented state, while ending effective representative government, controlling the press, restoring Catholicism under state control, reinstating colonial slavery and creating a hereditary monarchy and nobility. He legitimated his rule by plebiscite and the sovereignty of the people, pursued French pre-eminence by conscription and conquest, and used protection and the Continental System against Britain.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: At St Helena he said duties should guard a nation's trade and that he had not fallen into the error of 'modern systematizers' who condemned them; he ran state-directed trade policy. Evidence is about trade rather than markets in general, so low confidence.

property-fundamental.rationale: The 1804 Civil Code defined property as the right to enjoy and dispose of things in the most absolute manner (art. 544) and allowed taking only for public use with just prior indemnity (art. 545). His cadastre was described by him as the guarantee of property.

surveillance-ok.rationale: His letters to the police minister order arrests, prosecution of smugglers and watching of suspects, and he kept a political police; but his secretary reports he called the police dangerous for the ruler himself. Mixed, so low.

strong-leader.rationale: At St Helena he defended his dictatorship as absolutely necessary, said the concentration of power alone could save France, and in 1799 took power by coup. In his words: 'the State was myself'.

state-harmful.rationale: He built a centralized state (prefects, Council of State, Code, Concordat, university) and said the public welfare, 'the State', was himself.

empower-police-military.rationale: He expanded the army through conscription, ran a ministry of police under Fouché and reformed administration to concentrate power in the central government.

decide-locally.rationale: He reorganized local and regional administration to concentrate power in the central government.

traditional-family.rationale: The Code made the family a hierarchy under the husband and father (wife's obedience, paternal control, children's duty of respect), though it also allowed civil divorce.

more-religion-public.rationale: Through the 1801 Concordat he restored public Catholic worship and said he re-established religion as the foundation of sound principles and good morals.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He framed the Concordat partly as respect for the religion of the great majority and kept public ritual and honours, but he also abolished many revolutionary and older institutions. Mixed, so low.

gradual-change.rationale: He presented himself as the mediator between the old and new orders, reconciling the Revolution with what it had not destroyed, while remaking institutions across Europe by decree and conquest. Evidence points both ways.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He described a European congress and court of appeal with full powers over all states; but under French leadership.

free-trade.rationale: He imposed the Continental System, calling the prohibitive system the only way to make England sue for peace.

nation-first.rationale: At St Helena he said he had striven only for the glory, power and greatness of France.

revolution-justified.rationale: He seized power by coup and at St Helena called himself the heir who had purified the Revolution and said its cause had triumphed.

experts-over-public.rationale: He valued the Council of State of skilled, informed men and said the people's wishes are better read by the ruler than heard from them.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: He told political economists' critics that duties should be a protection of the nation matched to its trade, and told Sweden's Crown Prince that sovereigns would establish prohibitive laws. The Continental System shut British goods out of Europe and he promoted domestic cotton, sugar and indigo to replace imports.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He offered a prize of a million francs for a flax-spinning machine and promoted the domestic cultivation of sugar, indigo and cotton and cotton manufacture, ranking agriculture, then manufactures, then trade; these were state-driven efforts to build strategic industries.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The Code divides inheritances in equal portions among heirs and he defended the sale of confiscated national lands as a bulwark of the new order, but he also created large endowed estates for his marshals and regretted creating too many wealthy men. Mixed, so low.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: He established the Banque de France as France's first central bank.

one-party-rule.rationale: Inferred: from his stated aim to fuse and unite parties rather than rule through one; his regime had no governing party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: He had himself crowned Emperor in 1804 with a hereditary succession approved by plebiscite, and later wished to associate his son with him in the empire.

democracy-best.rationale: He ended directly elected representative government, ruled by plebiscite-approved dictatorship, and said licence and anarchy 'haunted the threshold of freedom'.

direct-votes.rationale: He had his constitution, consulship for life and hereditary empire put to plebiscites, though not individual laws, and sidelined the legislature; the plebiscites were also inflated. Mixed, so low.

natural-rulers.rationale: Inferred: from his statements that what the people say is scarcely ever what they want and that their wants are better read in the prince's heart, and that men are governed by fear and interest.

political-violence-never.rationale: He seized power in the 18 Brumaire coup, used the army against opponents and had the Duke d'Enghien tried and shot, which he defended.

war-builds-character.rationale: He said conscription becoming a point of honour makes a nation great and proof against reverses, and that danger excites Frenchmen. Said of service, not war in general.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Concordat and Organic Articles had the state nominate bishops, pay clergy and police worship; he said the police of religion should be entirely in the sovereign's hands.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The Civil Code is secular: civil marriage and divorce replaced canon law. He said religions are the work of men while valuing religion for social order.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred: from his construction of state courts, police and army as monopolies.

military-superiority.rationale: He built the Grande Armée and sought French pre-eminence in Europe, declaring that France's glory was his aim.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Inferred: from his stated belief in equality of rights and careers open to talent, alongside hereditary titles and rank.

civilizational-union.rationale: He said Europe would have become 'one and the same people' under common laws and institutions.

duties-before-rights.rationale: He said military service is a debt each person owes to his country, and valued honour and duty as the basis of national greatness.

restore-past-order.rationale: He restored religion and a nobility but rejected a Bourbon restoration and said he preserved the Revolution's gains.

results-over-ideology.rationale: He said he rejected the systematizers, adapted his projects to circumstances and called his religious policy a matter of social utility.

taxation-theft.rationale: He described the cadastre as a guarantee for individual security because the tax, once fixed by the legislature, could not be altered arbitrarily; taxation as such was treated as legitimate.

harm-principle.rationale: He restricted the press and religion's public use on grounds of order and the state's interests, not only harm to others.

conscription.rationale: He kept and expanded conscription; at St Helena he called it an eminently national institution and a debt to one's country.

total-state.rationale: His regime centralized education, press and administration and directed industry, but left property private.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He annexed and conquered territory across Europe to build an empire.

bound-labor.rationale: He abolished the vestiges of feudalism and feudal laws in France and conquered lands.

rule-by-example.rationale: He told Bourrienne men are governed only by fear and interest and said severity serves the ruler as well as mildness; he used laws and punishment.

national-self-determination.rationale: He re-created a Polish state (Duchy of Warsaw) and Italian kingdoms but conquered or installed rulers in Spain, Holland and Germany.

reason-over-faith.rationale: He said he could not believe what he was taught against his reason without hypocrisy and called his ambition the empire of reason, but he also valued religious sentiment as consoling and socially useful. Mixed, so low.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Code requires the wife's obedience to her husband (art. 213), bars her from suing, giving or acquiring without his authorization, and he joked that Europe had treated women too well and given them too much equality.

ban-interest.rationale: The Civil Code (arts. 1905-1907) declares it lawful to stipulate interest on loans and lets conventional interest exceed the legal rate.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: He banned the entry of Black people and people of mixed race into France, but the record shows no legal segregation of residence, schooling or facilities.

national-mission.rationale: He said he wanted to introduce France's doctrines, system of government and codes in the lands he took as a step toward the regeneration of Europe.

night-watchman-state.rationale: His state ran education, religion, trade policy, media and courts, far beyond defence, justice and property.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: He banned Black and mixed-race entry into France, yet at St Helena described considering polygamy and mixing in the colonies to reconcile Black welfare with colonial labour.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: His Code enacted equality before the law, but he reinstated slavery in 1802 and curtailed women's rights.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The Civil Code applied one body of civil law to all Frenchmen (art. 8) in place of feudal and local law; civil rights were declared independent of other status, and Protestants and Jews received civil and religious equality.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He said he reigned by the principle of the sovereignty of the people and held plebiscites on his regime, though results were inflated and he held that the people's wants are better read by their prince than heard from their mouths.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: He launched invasions of Egypt, Spain and Russia while claiming at St Helena that he had always received the first attack.

separated-powers.rationale: He said the concentration of power was what could save France and had a Senate and Council of State nominated by the executive; the legislative bodies had little independence.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: He argued that dictatorship was absolutely necessary amid anarchy and invasion, and said a military commission would have been legal for the Enghien affair.

party-controls-media.rationale: His decree of 1800 limited Paris to listed journals; his letters to the police minister direct what newspapers must say, forbid them to discuss priests, and propose closing one; the press was strictly controlled.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: At St Helena he described a plan for a European system with a common code, court of appeal with full powers, common weights, measures and money; but it was to be built under his leadership.

head-commands-forces.rationale: As First Consul and Emperor he personally commanded the armies and named the ministers; at St Helena he defended this concentration of authority.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The Concordat restored a hierarchical episcopal Catholic church (bishops nominated by him, instituted by the Pope, appointing parish priests) and he refused to found a Gallican church with himself as head.

clerical-rule.rationale: He subordinated the clergy to the civil government and appointed the bishops himself.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: His regime censored books, theatre and art, mainly for political ends; he also barred newspapers from discussing sacred subjects because he thought them unfit for such papers.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: He became consul for life in 1802 and Emperor with hereditary succession in 1804, with no limit on tenure.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He built permanent alliances and client states (Confederation of the Rhine, Austrian marriage) and kept armies of occupation abroad.

death-penalty.rationale: He kept the death penalty, had political opponents executed (the Duke d'Enghien) and told his brother Louis not to pardon criminals.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The Code makes the child of a Frenchman French even if born abroad (art. 10), while a child born in France to a foreigner may only claim French status after reaching majority (art. 9).

constituent-assembly.rationale: The 1799 constitution was drafted by a small group around Sieyes and himself and approved only by plebiscite, and later constitutional changes came by Senate decree, not an elected constituent assembly.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The Code treats ownership as an absolute right limited only by laws, with compulsory taking only for public good against indemnity; ownership is not framed as justified only by service to the common good.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Concordat left church lands unreturned, made bishops swear loyalty to the government and take state stipends, and the Organic Articles placed worship under state regulation; he said the control of religion belonged to the sovereign.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: He said he had united parties in France and aimed to be the natural mediator and arbiter between old and new orders.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: He sent an army to reassert control over Saint-Domingue in 1802, but at St Helena called that a great error and said he would have recognized its independence.

sacred-ruler.rationale: He denied imagining himself a son of a god after his Austrian marriage, saying sovereign power lies not in title or splendour.

leader-cult.rationale: His regime built a propaganda system of portraits, statues and mass praise around his image; The Legion of Honour and imperial court ceremonial added to it.

common-currency.rationale: His St Helena plan for Europe included money of the same value in different coins, plus common weights and measures.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The Continental System aimed to close European markets to Britain and make the continent self-sufficient in colonial goods, e.g. through domestic sugar, indigo and cotton, though he called it a wartime measure.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: He created a hereditary imperial nobility in 1806 with over 3,000 titles and said the Constituent Assembly was unwise to abolish titular nobility.

elective-rulers.rationale: He created a hereditary empire in place of an elected executive.

parliament-supreme.rationale: He dissolved the Legislative Body in 1813 when it opposed him, and said the Senate and legislative bodies mainly accommodated the urgency of the moment.

filial-duty.rationale: The Code states that a child at every age owes honour and respect to father and mother (art. 371) and that children owe maintenance to parents in need (art. 205).

office-by-exam.rationale: He filled posts by appointment with emphasis on talent, and set up competitive entry to elite schools, but not examinations for government posts as such.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: He argued in the Council of State for divorce on grounds of incompatibility and said limiting it to proven adultery would abolish it; the Code allows divorce by mutual consent, though with strict conditions.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The Code makes property in land an absolute individual right (art. 544) rather than a holding conditional on use; this follows directly from the text he enacted.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: He described the cadastre tax as fixed and established by the legislature; but the legislature under his rule voted with little independence.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: He sent troops into Portugal and Spain in 1808, deposed Spain's rulers and installed his brother in order to enforce his trade embargo and alliance system.

non-intervention.rationale: He intervened in other states' internal affairs: he deposed Spain's rulers in 1808, installed relatives as kings, and described himself as aspiring to be arbiter of nations and kings.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The Civil Code makes marriage a civil institution with property and legal consequences.

religious-nation.rationale: His regime recognized Catholics, Protestants and Jews and he said he treated the religious minority with equality so that differences would fade; the nation was not defined by a shared religion.

religion-illusion.rationale: He called religions human works and said religion supplies something marvellous that people crave, but called belief a consolation and a gift of Heaven and believed in God. Points both ways.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He closed most opposition newspapers, issued a January 1800 decree allowing only listed journals, and exiled or imprisoned critics.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: He retook Saint-Domingue for its wealth, reinstated slavery, and described Egypt as a colony to take the place of Saint-Domingue; he also wished the colonies to supply France with goods.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: He said he united parties and became the mediator between the old and new orders, maintaining the principles of both.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: He said he could reign only by the principle of the sovereignty of the people, which excluded the Bourbons' claims. He nonetheless had himself crowned Emperor in 1804.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He built the largest army in Europe and described it as the guarantee of French greatness.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The 1804 empire was made hereditary and he named his son as heir (King of Rome), planning to associate him with the throne.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: He enacted a published Code he praised for its simplicity, but he also ruled by decree and used special commissions and imprisonment of suspects. Points both ways.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: He summoned a Sanhedrin in 1807 to adapt the law of Moses to the laws of the empire.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: He restored religious worship, said he built on religion as the support of morality, and rejected the Revolution's atheistic campaigns.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: He built the state's police and prisons; his letters order arrests and imprisonment of suspects.

term-limits.rationale: He made himself consul for life and then hereditary Emperor.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The Code gives the husband authority: he owes protection and the wife owes obedience (art. 213) and her legal acts need his concurrence.

second-chamber.rationale: His constitutions provided a Senate alongside the Legislative Body and Tribunate, and in 1815 he accepted a Chamber of Peers beside the Chamber of Representatives.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred: from conscription, which he called a debt each person owes the country, and his statement that the state was himself.

spiritual-nature.rationale: He said people's minds need the undefined and marvellous that religion offers, and treated religion as a necessary part of the social order.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred: from his reorganization of local government into centrally appointed prefects with no autonomy of their own.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: He said that after peace he would have proclaimed all future wars defensive and aggrandizement anti-national, and that he always received the first attack, but his record includes invasions of Spain, Portugal and Russia.

arms-reduction.rationale: He said that after peace the great standing armies would be cut down to sovereigns' guards; as a stated plan at St Helena, not practice.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: His letters order the arrest of deserting conscripts and measures against evasion.

public-service-media.rationale: His regime controlled the press, books and theatre rather than allowing independent media.

religions-one-truth.rationale: He said all religions are plainly the work of men, contradict and persecute each other, and that priests everywhere introduced fraud.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The Code gives children equal shares without distinction of sex, but a married woman cannot alienate or acquire without her husband's authority. Mixed.

women-suffrage.rationale: Women had no vote or public office under his constitutions and he joked at St Helena that women had been treated too well and allowed to rank as equals, and historians note he reduced women's civil rights.

indirect-election.rationale: His 1799 constitution chose the Legislative Body and Tribunate from indirectly elected candidates, with the Senate and Council of State effectively nominated by the executive.

national-church-status.rationale: The Concordat recognized Catholicism as the religion of the great majority and restored its public worship with state support, but Protestants and Jews were also recognized and paid; it did not make Catholicism an exclusive state religion.

equal-conscription.rationale: Napoleonic conscription applied to men only.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred: from his 1802 reinstatement of slavery and conscription of every man.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: He said he sought to unite and amalgamate parties, relied on appointed bodies and plebiscites, and described himself as above factions.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The Code lets wives petition for divorce on specified grounds (for husband's adultery only if he kept a concubine in the marital home), so a husband's consent is not required, but the grounds are unequal; he also wanted limits on women's repeat divorces.

multipolar-world.rationale: He admitted aspiring to a 'universal Dictatorship' and an arbiter's role among nations.

notes: Answers rest on his recorded St Helena conversations (mediated by Las Cases, written after defeat and shaped by self-justification), his letters, and the laws and decrees of his regime. Some of his statements conflict with his record (e.g. 'defensive wars only' and the European plan versus his conquests); these are answered 0 or low. Plebiscite results were inflated. Answers marked 'Inferred:' are low confidence and follow directly from stated views or enacted measures.
